subject: gate
text: gate-a (cheap tier, haiku) reliably fails to complete on a large accumulated diff (~164 files): its correction loop must regenerate the full findings+checked list from scratch each retry, and drops a different handful of files each attempt, never converging within the 2-correction budget. Seen 4/4 times on vendeya-tenant-foundation (chatbot), a long-lived task with many uncommitted rounds. Gate B (also cheap tier) has not shown this failure mode on the same diff. Mitigated per-round via the documented 'edit a tier for that one round' escape hatch (CAP_ROLE_GATE_A=standard env override), not a permanent config change. Worth considering: scale gate-a's correction budget or tier with diff size, or land intermediate commits more often on long-lived tasks so --full never has to re-review the whole accumulated diff at once.

subject: gate
text: Background 'cap gate' invocations for vendeya-tenant-foundation were killed 4 times in a row by the harness's low-memory guard ('system is running low on memory'), each time at a similar free-memory level (~1.1-1.4Gi free, ~4.7-5.0Gi available per free -h) that did not look like genuine host distress and did not change even after the kill. Each dispatched review session (even cheap-tier haiku) also loads the full MCP server set (context7-mcp, etc.) unconditionally via claude_settings/launch in caplib.py, adding ~100-250MB of sidecar processes per session that a git-diff-only review does not need. Worth checking: (1) whether the background-task low-memory monitor's threshold is too conservative relative to Linux's own 'available' accounting, (2) whether dispatched review/gate sessions could skip MCP server loading (e.g. via a lean settings profile) to shrink their footprint.
